ledger.claim: The rider does not contest the two limbs this record actually decides, and does not ask for a refund on either: under POL-NS-23 the driver sent in-app messages at 08:04:40 and 08:08:30 and placed an in-app call at 08:07:10, all before the 08:10:05 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met; and under POL-NS-21 the free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 08:04:20 and expired at 08:09:20, 45 s before the cancellation, so the wait was served. The rider's side puts its case on the point below rather than on those limbs.

The 5.00 SGD fee should be held rather than collected. This is an on-demand trip and the record's own derived driver_deadline carries deadline null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time', so the arrival deadline POL-NS-24 fixes cannot be computed on this record, and the category's own note directs POL-GEN-26 where the deadline cannot be fixed. POL-NS-26 makes the AI's no-show ruling final only 'subject to POL-GEN-26', and ESCALATE under POL-GEN-03 goes to a human reviewer with no monetary outcome and the amount held, which is the only outcome on this record that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

Admissibility is asymmetric here in a way that matters, and it is disclosed as such: the only artifact below full weight is the traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-05051-01, which is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, so the record carries no third-party account of the conditions at the pickup during the wait. Every timing fact on which the charge turns is computed from an automated arrival event and the driver's own device trace, whose rider_track is empty, leaving the margin of 45 s uncorroborated from any independent source; under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact, and under POL-GEN-26 a case that cannot be established on the evidence that would carry it is held for review, not decided on the driver's device alone.

The driver's arrival at the pickup is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace and is a complete artifact at weight 1.0: the nearest fix sits 3.74 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 4 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace then holds zero-speed fixes continuously from 08:04:31 to 08:10:01. The driver stopped at the pickup at 08:04:20 and did not leave it.

This is an on-demand trip (scheduled_at is null), so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 08:04:20 and expires at 08:09:20. The driver cancelled at 08:10:05 — 345 s after arrival, 45 s past the expiry of the free wait. The cancellation was therefore made after the free wait had run out, not during it.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met twice over. The driver sent in-app chat messages at 08:04:40 and 08:08:30, and placed an in-app call at 08:07:10 that rang 25 s unanswered. Both a message and a call precede the 08:10:05 cancellation, and the derived contact check scores complete=true and obligation_met=true. There is no basis to void the fee.

The rider's own account and conduct put the no-show on her side. She states in her claim that she 'came down maybe 2 minutes late'; the driver's two messages were read at 08:05:14 and 08:08:50, so she knew the driver was waiting; and her only reply came at 08:11:40 — 'sorry coming now, where are you' — more than 90 s after the driver had cancelled. She was not at the pickup at any point during the free wait, and the fee follows from that absence under POL-NS-22.

The driver-no-show limb in POL-NS-24 does not bite. The record carries no scheduled pickup time (scheduled_at null), so there is no 'scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes' deadline for the driver to have missed, and on an on-demand trip the free wait runs from arrival, which the driver satisfied. Nor is the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit due: that credit requires both a missed deadline and a failure to attempt contact, and here the driver both messaged and called.

The amount charged is exactly the fee the no-show policy fixes: 5.00 SGD, with fee_matches_policy true, the ledger reconciling to total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — nothing has yet been returned to the rider. Under POL-NS-22 the fee stands and is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, so the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00, as POL-GEN-03 requires.

No escalation is warranted. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile snapshot carries a fraud_flags entry, so the 0.95 bar is not engaged; and POL-NS-26 makes the ruling on a no-show final at the fixed 5.00 SGD fee. The case is decidable on this record.

POL-GEN-26 does not call for escalation here, because every fact the no-show rules need is established on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0: the arrival time, the two messages, the in-app call, the cancellation time and the fee. The only MISSING artifact is the traffic advisory (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), which under POL-GEN-02(3) carries no fact, and no rule in this category turns on it. There is accordingly no open question to send to a reviewer.

The repeat no-show referral in POL-NS-25 does not fire on this trip: that rule applies only where the optional rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d counter is present, and the rider's profile snapshot for this trip does not carry it. No referral naming POL-NS-25 arises.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This is the no-show charge on trip TRP-05051. The 5.00 SGD fee stands and is payable to the driver; the rider's request to waive it is refused.

What the record shows. The trip was on-demand, and on an on-demand trip the 5-minute free wait runs from the driver's arrival (POL-NS-21). The driver's device trace (EV-GPS-05051, complete, weight 1.0) corroborates arrival at the pickup at 08:04:20 — nearest fix 3.74 m out with 4 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and shows the car stationary there from 08:04:31 until 08:10:01. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05051, weight 1.0) shows the driver messaged the rider at 08:04:40 and 08:08:30 (both read) and placed an in-app call at 08:07:10 that rang 25 s unanswered, then cancelled at 08:10:05 — 345 s after arriving, 45 s after the 300 s free wait expired at 08:09:20. The rider's only reply, 'sorry coming now, where are you', came at 08:11:40, after the cancellation. The payments ledger (EV-FARE-05051, weight 1.0) shows 5.00 SGD charged, exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, with nothing refunded.

Why the fee stands. Both rider-favouring limbs are satisfied: the driver served the free wait (POL-NS-21) and met the contact obligation — a message and a call, both before cancelling (POL-NS-23). The charge is the exact 5.00 SGD of POL-NS-22, so it is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. Under POL-GEN-03 that is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying the same 5.00 figure.

On the rider's arguments for holding the money:
- POL-GEN-26 / the unfixable 'scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes' deadline. I do not escalate on this. POL-NS-24's deadline is the test for a driver no-show, and an on-demand trip has no scheduled time (the record's own driver_deadline shows deadline null for that reason). But POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established from the evidence that would carry it. Here every needed fact is established on complete weight-1.0 artifacts: when the driver arrived (08:04:20, GPS-corroborated), whether he messaged and called before cancelling (he did, both), and the fee (5.00). The driver arrived and waited out the free wait, so there is no driver-lateness question left open.
- The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05051-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) and the empty rider_track. The advisory carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)) and no rule in this category turns on it, so its absence raises no open question. The empty rider_track does not impair the driver-device trace, which is complete, and the 45 s between the free wait's expiry and the cancellation is covered by that trace's zero-speed fixes from 08:04:31 to 08:10:01.

No referral arises. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag needs rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, which this snapshot does not carry. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit needs both a missed arrival deadline and a failure to attempt contact; neither is present. POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral needs a fee other than 5.00 SGD; the fee is exactly 5.00. Confidence is 0.95: the contested sum is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, no fraud flag is engaged on either profile, and every deciding fact rests on complete weight-1.0 artifacts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
